items.item_text: Pharmacy Technician License in the State of California
Pharmacy Technician Certification (CPhT)
Minimum education satisfied through attainment of the required licensure/certification
At least 4 years of recent Outpatient Pharmacy experience as a Pharmacy Technician
Previous Supervisory experience in a pharmacy setting
Experience training or mentoring staff, serving as a technical resource, coordinating workflow, resolving operational issues, or supporting daily operations
Experience working at a UCDH Outpatient/Specialty Pharmacy
Experience working in a Health System Pharmacy or Specialty Pharmacy
Experience in Epic Willow Ambulatory Outpatient Dispensing system
Experience in MS Office Suite: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Access
Experience with bargaining units and labor relations
Experience ensuring compliance of operations to specialty pharmacy accrediting bodies (i.e. URAC, TJC, ACHC, etc.)

UCDH Outpatient pharmacies emphasize patient care in Hospital Discharge, Oncology, Infectious Diseases, Ambulatory Care, Employee Health and Specialty Pharmacy. Our pharmacies are responsible for screening prescriptions for appropriateness and making interventions, preparing medications for dispensing, distribution activities, providing immunizations and providing patient consultations. Staff are responsible for appropriate prescription billing to multiple payers including third party insurances, Medicaid, Medicare D and Medicare B plans. Our pharmacies maintain compliance with multiple accrediting bodies and with State and Federal Laws and Regulations.
90% - Pharmacy Operations Supervision
This position supervises Pharmacy Technicians in our Pharmacy Department and is an integral member of the healthcare team.
10% - Pharmacy Operations Support and Tasks

Our Technician Supervisors are responsible for the supervision and support of their assigned direct reports. This position is responsible for supervision of their direct reports which involves timecard activities, performance management, training, scheduling, conducting meetings with staff and others, and creating, maintaining and having oversight of daily operations and workflows.

Based on operations, there may be other responsibilities such as, but not limited to, providing drug dispensing and distribution activities, compounding prescriptions, maintaining pharmacy robotics, inventory management, pharmacy maintenance, customer service (via telephone, electronic and in-person), prescription data entry, insurance adjudication and troubleshooting, processing prescription payments and more.

This position is highly collaborative with direct reports, peers and other leaders and requires participation in meetings within pharmacy and stakeholders external to pharmacy. This position fosters excellent intra- and interdepartmental relationships and provides quality and cost-effective pharmaceutical care to all patients. #CA-DS
Must be able to accurately perform pharmacy calculations
Working knowledge in billing current third-party insurances, Medicare Part B and California State Medicaid
Current working knowledge of pharmacy terminology, generic/brand names and drug abbreviations
Working knowledge in submitting authorization requests for medications
Working knowledge of current Medi-Cal Formulary and other third-party billing systems.
Working knowledge of current California Pharmacy Law
Ability to recognize situations that exceed technician authority and must be referred to a pharmacist for resolution.
Ability to operate Pharmacy Information System and other computer programs

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem and identify the resources available to help solve the problem; ability to independently create and implement viable solutions and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved.
Ability to exercise discretion to ensure that patient confidentiality is maintained, and a professional, respectful clinic/department environment exists at all times.
Ability to impart knowledge and develop the skills of students participating in training programs, as well as new hires and staff seeking additional opportunities.
Working knowledge of and skill to apply practices, principles and techniques of patient care related to area of expertise.

Written and oral communication skills to clearly and concisely provide information, explanations and instructions to, and to elicit information from others with varying levels of ability to understand, including individuals who are ill or distressed, or who may not speak English
